threads.body: The poisoning, the hatchlings, and the first cracks in the family. What did you trust by the end of this chapter?
The escape plan is one thing. What did the family confrontation change about how you read the brothers?
Jace the Hand: a promotion, a responsibility, or another way to keep a son inside the king’s reach? Discuss Chapter III here.
The knight’s survival and the Hand’s first work in a restless court: which side of the chapter stayed with you?
Oldtown and the cost of the king’s retribution. Please keep the people harmed in view as well as the princes.
Paranoia at home, fragile hope in Dorne, and Alester’s return. How do those threads change each other?
A mountain climb and a knight’s vows: what does earning a bond look like in this chapter?
Power, a new dragonrider, and the threat behind the tourney preparations. Spoilers stop at Chapter VIII.
The lists finally turn the brothers’ rivalry into a public result. Match reactions, character readings and terrible imaginary predictions welcome.
After the violence of the lists, what does the recovery chapter actually repair?
Visenor’s journey north and the argument about justice back in the capital. What do you think the pact is buying?
The Trial: sentence, legitimacy, and the gap between what the Crown calls justice and what Costayne will accept.
The judgment’s aftermath and the private confrontations it produces. How much authority does the Hand really have?
An uncomfortable reunion and an old Riverlands feud. Which conversation did you most want to escape?
The Glass Flower: the gift, the perspective, and what Alester can and cannot offer. This thread may discuss the whole chapter.
The Mummer’s Blood: inherited temper, performance, and old dragon lore. What changed for you after the flashback?

threads.title: Ghost dragon theories: camouflage is not invisibility
threads.body: What can the lore conversation actually support? Current-chapter spoilers; distinguish a theory from an established trait.

threads.title: Hot take: the quiet chapters are doing the heavy lifting
threads.body: I remember the missing-person conversations and the window more clearly than some of the big collisions. Do you want more breathing room, or does the pace work for you?

threads.title: The extremely unofficial impossible-pairing desk
threads.body: No endgame predictions. No fake receipts. Just combinations the notes app has decided to care about. Keep it non-explicit and let people dislike a pairing without making it personal.

threads.title: Which council meeting should have been a raven?
threads.body: Current-chapter spoilers. Choose one meeting you would have escaped, or defend the need for everyone to be in the same room.

threads.title: What are you eating while reading? Crumbs are already in the book.
threads.body: I made the mistake of bringing something flaky to my reread. What is everyone having? This is a snack thread, not a test of whether your dinner is sufficiently medieval.

threads.title: Did an edit give you completely the wrong first impression?
threads.body: Not asking editors to submit a sworn statement. I mean when a crop, a reaction shot or the order of clips makes you expect a different person before you read. What do you notice once you go back to the source?

threads.title: Modern AU: give someone an ordinary job they would actually keep
threads.body: No king, CEO or assassin. I want a job with a rota and a slightly broken kettle. Entirely non-canon. Bonus points if they could make it through probation.

threads.title: A take you have actually changed your mind about
threads.body: A real one. Not "I thought my favourite was great but they are even greater". You can also have liked something less on a reread. No compulsory redemption arc for your opinion.

threads.title: Small questions desk: names, navigation, things you lost track of
threads.body: Ask the thing you think everyone else already knows. Please say which chapter you have reached so replies do not ruin the next one. No need to apologise for mixing up a name.

threads.title: The Great Game table: are you building to win or refusing to cut your favourite?
threads.body: I can tell myself a card belongs in the plan for a suspiciously long time when I like the character. Talk deckbuilding habits, favourite picks and bad decisions here. If you suggest a specific interaction, check the actual card text first.

threads.title: Can we have one dragon thread without making a tier list?
threads.body: Favourite details, questions about habitat, a design you like. Anything except turning every trait into who beats whom. Unconfirmed ideas are welcome if you label them as ideas.

threads.title: One ordinary afternoon from a side character: who gets the page?
threads.body: Not a reveal chapter or a secret mastermind pitch. Pick someone whose ordinary day you would like to understand. What would their attention settle on that the princes would miss?

Chapter XVII: The Children Pay. Rhaella's death, Visenor at Highgarden, the Starfall mystery, the forged letter and the council aftermath. Full Chapter XVII spoilers; discussion includes sexual violence and death. Bring your reactions and theories, but leave graphic quotations out of replies.

comments.body:
The last words are an accusation, not a solved case. Gaelor kills the person who might have explained them.

That is the interesting failure to me: he obtains information and destroys the possibility of checking it in the same scene.
the hand. two words. derrin discourse has entered the building

The kitchen executions are where the opening lands for me. The servants become disposable because the king is frightened. Saera argues for their lives; Jace also argues that you cannot run a kingdom like this. Neither argument saves them.
three hatchlings arrive and they immediately become an allocation dispute. incredible family
i like that the celebration and the panic happen together. the dragons do not pause their lives for a succession crisis
so the last words give us a suspect, not the whole conspiracy?
Correct. At this chapter boundary, we have the accusation and the letter concerning Rhaella; neither establishes the full poisoning conspiracy.
jace helping visenor off the floor before everything turns strategic again. that is the bit i keep thinking about

Dorne versus Essos is not just the helpful brother offering a better holiday. Jace understands that an exiled claimant can become someone else’s weapon.

The rescue is compassionate and controlling at once. I like not having to choose only one reading.
alester leaving the guards breathing matters. the escape does not become another excuse to kill everyone in the corridor
Rhaella asking whether there would have been a marriage without the letters is painful. That is a person trying to find out which part of her life is real.
the cover story has one source of truth and approximately a million ways to fail
bring lorenah to court. simple work trip. nothing else happened. normal expense report
Jace getting the Hand position makes sense to me. He is already thinking about what holds the family and the court together, even while he is terrified about the people he sent away.
Being good at keeping this court together is not automatically a compliment. The machinery itself is the problem. He is being promoted inside it.
sure but somebody still has to make decisions tomorrow morning. being capable of that is not nothing
I did not say it was nothing. I am saying competence has a direction. Who benefits when the machine runs more smoothly?
and i think the chapter leaves that question open. the stuff with vhaemys makes him feel like a person trying to protect people, not a walking institution
The Vhaemys scene works on me too. That is why I want to separate affection from governing. A man can be tender with his family and still preserve something ugly.
okay that is fair. i read your first reply as saying the appointment tells us nothing about him
It tells us a lot. I just do not think all of it is flattering. Also yes, I did feel something when he admitted missing Alester. Annoying of the story.
Promotion discourse aside, someone now has to carry the administration while everybody else manufactures emergencies. The job is not only the pin.
Vhaemys looking for Alester gives his absence a life outside the escape plot. Other people have lost their ordinary routines too.
Gaelor hears the confession himself. What a reader knows at the end of this chapter and what the court can establish are still different questions.
i like the small missing-alester conversation more than the promotion. the title is big, the absence feels specific
i came here to say alester needs rest and ended up rereading the title for ten minutes
Loyalty has a physical cost here. It is easy for a court to discuss an oath as if the person fulfilling it never needs to stop.
The Master of Coin is asking what happens after the victory. That is a real question, not cowardice. Taking money and immediately putting it into another war is not a recovery plan.
Jace calling the campaign a message to the whole realm is why I resist the harmless clever-prince reading. He understands the intimidation and can make its case.
the first days of a new job but the job is making everyone remember their place
i liked moving between the court and the people actually trying to survive. the contrast makes the confident council talk sound different
The language of royal authority does not make this less of a massacre. A command moving down the hierarchy does not remove the choices of the person carrying it out.
i am not defending what happened to the people at oldtown. i still think the father-son part matters if we are talking about how gaelor got here
Explanation matters. It just does not have to become exoneration. The title invites the inherited-pattern reading without requiring us to forgive the son.
Saathos being loyal cannot be the end of the conversation about Saathos either. I follow him separately from Gaelor, and that means looking at the ugly parts too.
this is where the scale of the cruelty starts crowding out the individual people for me. i wanted more space with them before the prince becomes the centre of the discussion again
i understand that. for me the horror is that the court can turn all of those lives into a political consequence. i do not think being horrified means the scene failed
The people who suffer do not have to become useful lessons for the ruling family to matter.
Jace worrying about what Vhaemys is learning from the king is a much more interesting concern than deciding the child is already beyond help. She is watching the adults.
yes. getting her a different influence is an actual response, not just being upset that she copies him
training with someone who can still challenge you is good. being surrounded by people who only tell you how impressive you are is not training
alester kneeling when he should barely be standing. i would like to personally remove oaths from the room for five minutes
That ending makes loyalty feel both beautiful and frightening. I can admire the devotion and want someone to tell him he has done enough.
the dorne sections gave me enough breathing room to finish this one. i needed somewhere in the story that still allowed hope
visenor packing actual supplies before going up the mountain. a rare win for preparation enthusiasts
Food, water, rope, blankets. I appreciate a dangerous journey that remembers a body has ordinary requirements.
boneskin not immediately deciding the silver-haired man is his best friend. respect
The waiting and shared food matter more to me than the idea of blood as an instant access pass. He has to stay with an animal that has its own reasons to be wary.
the climb and the kneeling feel like two ways of having to earn something rather than just being born near it
coming back and telling the whole journey over wine is such a good release after the climb
Cordin presenting terror as fifteen years of peace tells us how he sells the reign. I would not automatically adopt his definition of peace as the narrator’s verdict.
A deterrent can prevent wars. That is not a ridiculous argument simply because Cordin makes it.
Preventing open war and making ordinary people safe are different measures. The account of peace needs to include whose fear is doing the work.
Boneskin refusing to leave the egg makes the relocation a negotiation. The dragon has a priority that is not Visenor’s title.
the council working out how to sell a war as liberation is bleak. they know exactly which values they need to borrow
ending on dark sister in the room is more than enough threat for me. no theory essay. just dread
By the end I am less interested in who won than who let the tilt keep turning into this. The horses did not sign up for the family argument.
both men stop behaving like they are trying to win a normal match. the crowd gets a spectacle and nobody gets a sensible decision
Gaelor staying mounted is the result. It does not settle every hypothetical sword fight or prove Jace has never trained. Different contest.
yes he fell. i have accepted this. please stop sending my imaginary inbox the same result
i would like the record to show that i have sent zero messages and thought about it several times
Costayne appearing here means Oldtown has a survivor who can act, not just a memory for the princes to process. That changes the scene for me.
alester/godfrey corner has received crumbs. this is a fan interpretation, please do not summon the evidence committee
Putting two injured sons near each other does not repair their relationship. The king can command proximity much more easily than trust.
the quiet hurts more because nobody has suddenly become good at talking
i liked slowing down after the tourney. if every chapter immediately reaches for the next collision, the injuries stop feeling like anything
same on the slowdown. i am less sold on asking the exhausted-father image to carry sympathy without sitting longer with how he made this situation
for me the fireflies give the moment tenderness without making it forgiveness
Steffon winning by default while the two people everyone watched destroy each other is a very funny footnote to a miserable day.
the carved boneskin gift was a nice moment before my anxiety returned to full-time employment
The nameday starts with something personal and ends up entangled with claims and alliances again. Even the peaceful moments have politics waiting outside the door.
Jace suggesting trial by combat is not a neutral explanation of available procedure if he also knows who will step into the circle. The advice has an intended consequence.
Costayne asking what justice approves of killing children challenges the legitimacy of the court itself. It is not just an appeal for a lighter sentence.
oldtown. citadel. a new set of doors to knock on. i remain convinced the hightower part of this story has more to give
More story is plausible. That does not establish any particular comeback theory.
prove yourself in war, then everyone will accept you. that bargain feels like it can always demand one more war
The Wall sentence matters because Jace is trying to exercise authority without simply giving Gaelor the ending he wants. That does not mean Costayne accepts the institution that hands it down.
he tried to kill a prince. twice. everyone keeps writing around that as though it is a minor administrative issue
Nobody needs to erase the attempts to ask whether this court is impartial. The political history is part of why the defendant rejects its claim to justice.
and the victims of his revenge are just meant to wait while we workshop the philosophy?
That is not what I wrote. You are arguing with the easiest version of the point rather than the one in front of you.
you are genuinely too stupid to read a plain sentence when a prince you dislike is in it
You can call the sentence wrong. You can call my decisions wrong. Calling another reader stupid is where this stops. Rule 1: argue the take, not the person. Keep the next reply on the chapter.
fine. my actual objection is that the sentence does not answer the second attempt on gaelor. that is what i wanted addressed
That is a specific objection I can answer. My reading is that the sentence contains him; it is not an agreement that his revenge was justified.
A sentence can end a proceeding without restoring anyone’s belief in justice. Costayne’s final insistence makes that divide very clear.
everyone in this room is using the word justice for a different thing and insisting the others know exactly what they mean
i found the mess more convincing than a clean victory for jace. i can also see why someone would find it frustrating to read
The Crown and the Faith are not interchangeable voices here. The competing claims to legitimate judgment are the point worth following.
this thread has helped me separate the actual sentence from what costayne thinks of it. thanks
having the office and being allowed to use it are clearly not the same problem
management would like you to take responsibility but not make any decisions it dislikes
The confrontation makes the title feel conditional. Baelenys can demand a strong Hand and still experience independent judgment as a challenge to himself.
The ghost-dragon descendant is a lead at this point, not an identified creature. I like the possibility of old stories becoming politically useful again.
a rumour can be useful before anyone knows if it is true. finally a chapter understands my workflow
Useful is not verified. I am putting that underneath this one in advance.
the title promises something broken and the office really does feel less secure by the end. that part worked for me
The Blackwood account is still an account from an interested party. Jace asking what the Crown can establish is not the same as proving the death was accidental.
And Tully’s marriage connection complicates the apparently easy answer of asking the liege lord to settle it. The chapter makes the available channels feel compromised.
the riverlands have brought a centuries-old household argument to somebody else’s desk
Tariffs, fishing rights, then a demand to authorize a war. Very normal progression for the morning queue.
the reunion title sounds so much gentler than the experience of reading this family in a room
lorenah playing the harp is one of the details i was happy to linger on. she has a life when the princes are busy

Alester wants to give Saera something extraordinary, but he cannot control what the restored sight means to her.

That is why the window hurts. His effort and her happiness do not arrange themselves into the story he might have wanted.
The flower breaking makes the gift feel temporary before the emotional meaning has even settled. I do not read it as a simple punishment for loving someone.
Rickard saying what a princess ultimately desires is Rickard making a claim. Saera does not become an equation that either man has solved because he speaks confidently.
yes. i can feel bad for alester without turning saera into someone who owes him the correct reaction
this is the kind of damage i find more effective than another body count. the chapter lets several people want different things in the same small space
personally this is one of my favourites. i get why the symbolism could feel heavy to someone else but the emotional situation carried it for me
The proposal and the northern section both ask what being chosen actually means, but in very different registers. I liked reading them together.
Seeing the young Baelenys makes the later family patterns harder to treat as isolated outbursts. A flashback can explain a shape without forgiving what it becomes.
i understand the parallel. i still wanted more time with the performers before another royal reaction becomes the main event. that criticism is about emphasis, not me missing that gaelor is cruel
i read the performance as people briefly getting to speak back to power, which is why the response hurt. but wanting more of them as people is a fair criticism
The dragon-lore conversation is careful about camouflage versus literal transparency. Those are different claims. I would keep that distinction in any ghost-dragon theory.
yes, colour and light can explain the account without immediately inventing invisibility powers
zekar, mydan, merryn. i want to remember the names and not just call this the gaelor scene
Not everything should become an argument about whether a follower had better intentions than his prince. The people on the other end still experience the violence.
came for the lore. stayed for the very bad feeling.
The account gives us colour, texture and changing light. I would start there before adding a power the conversation does not establish.
counterpoint: the phrase ghost dragon is doing excellent marketing work on me
That is fair as atmosphere. I am only resisting the leap from a striking name to a confirmed supernatural mechanism.
so my elaborate diagram currently proves that i own a pen
I think the collisions make the quiet moments matter more, but I do not need every ending to escalate. Fireflies worked for me precisely because it stayed with the aftermath.
yeah personally i like the balance more than em does. but if someone asks for more time with side characters, answering that they just cannot handle tragedy is dodging the point
my draft said skill issue. i have chosen growth today
rare good patch notes from this account
The question for me is whether a scene changes how I understand a person. Quiet or loud is less important than whether the change feels earned.
alester/godfrey remains in the folder. i am asking for zero changes to canon and several hours of my own free time
two shared frames is a luxury in this economy
i do not see that pairing at all but i respect the commitment to saying it is your invention
headcanon labelled as headcanon. the filing department is briefly at peace
If a meeting authorizes another war, I unfortunately want the people controlling the money in the room. The raven can carry the apology for how long it takes.
please stop putting the same person in charge of the incident and the incident report
If I send the raven, someone asks for a meeting to discuss the raven.
first useful management statement i have seen all week
cake. but i ate the top first
soup and a chapter on my break. luxurious until the break ends
the chapter gets longer as the break gets shorter. known phenomenon
Tea and biscuits here. Put a little plate underneath, dear. Saves the keyboard.
the plate has another cake on it
opened this for meal ideas and realised i forgot lunch
Toast counts. Go and make some before another chapter.
my keyboard has a geological record
leaving this thread open as evidence that plates have been explained
i know what plates are jace

A reaction shot moved three seconds can make someone look like they planned the whole conversation. That is the part I keep checking.

I still enjoy an edit with a point of view. I just want to know when my memory of the scene is actually my memory of the edit.
sometimes i know it is misleading and watch it six more times. the mood got me
Worth keeping the chapter reference in a caption when possible. Lets people find the scene without asking the same question under every repost.
reels with homework. we have lost the war
a reference is not an assignment. you can keep scrolling
oh. i have definitely been remembering a caption as dialogue
the worst part is being very confident about it until someone asks which chapter
Saathos: the shift supervisor who knows which cupboard has the working equipment. People ignore him until something breaks.
that is the person management calls indispensable immediately before refusing the pay rise
Alester on overnight reception. you get the key, you get the directions, nobody demands your life story
jace would last one shift before trying to reorganise the rota
And discover that three people have the same name in the payroll export.
The cupboard is labelled. This has not helped.

i used to think a quiet scene was automatically doing more character work. sometimes it is just repeating something we already know, slower.

still want more breathing room. i am less impressed by breathing room as an argument on its own.
i agree with that more than i expected. although repetition can show someone is stuck rather than the story being stuck
sure. but at some point i need a different consequence, not another reminder that they are miserable
fair. i think i have sometimes treated recognising an intention as the same thing as liking the result
yeah that is where i land too. i can see what a scene is going for and still wish it landed differently
two critics agreeing. thread is washed
we agreed on one sentence. please respect our privacy
i used to treat wanting a happier outcome as proof the sad ending worked. sometimes yes. sometimes i just wanted another possibility to feel like it had a chance.
not a plot question but does anyone else keep the family tree open the entire time
family tree, chapter, character profile, unrelated tab i cannot explain. yes
I keep notes on paper. This is not a superior method; I have now misplaced the paper.
A bookmark helps more than my elaborate notebook ever did. Start with the people in the scene; the rest can wait.
collecting favourites and making a sensible deck are two separate hobbies that keep charging me the same attention
i want the boring support piece to get credit when it makes the whole thing function
then when i win i will say it was strategic and when i lose i will say it was a theme deck. covered both exits
my favourite archetype is blaming the draw
Write down why you kept the hand before you see the result. Much harder to retrofit a genius explanation afterwards.
ranking the thread premise C tier
you have been here for twelve seconds
i like looking at how much space an animal that size would need. makes every building around it feel temporary
can we have a little dragon garden
The fence would have a very short career.
i do actually want more of the size comparison stuff. not to pick a winner. i am bad at picturing numbers
someone who has to clean the room after the dramatic exit. i want to know how late they get home
the person fixing a damaged sleeve while everyone talks over them. they are trying to match thread, not interpret a prophecy
I would read that. Especially if they misread the grand conversation because they have a more urgent problem of their own.
Yes. Let an ordinary person have incomplete information without making them foolish. Readers already know more than any one person in the room.
coming back to this: a pause can change what i am hoping for, even if it does not change what happened. that is the useful kind of breathing room for me.
put the decision at the top of the raven. if i have to scroll to find out why i am here i am already against it
update: the alester/godfrey folder now has a playlist. evidence remains unchanged.
i have revised the diagram. it now says maybe in a larger font.
started as a way to keep the chapters and family tree in one place. then apparently nobody knew when to stop adding tabs.
so i can be confused in several beautifully indexed locations instead of one 👍
beautiful subtavern yes. i am withholding "best admins in the known world" pending several peer reviews.
Finally, a thread with standards.
you found this thread suspiciously fast
correct answer. i will remember this philosophy right up until i lose twice and start moving cards around like furniture.
building for fun until the first extremely avoidable loss changes my entire personality for six minutes
because that is exactly what I said when the fifth tab appeared.
I prefer 'efficiently informed.'
I cannot confirm the administrators, but Adana is now the leading theory in this thread.
same. I am here for the snack audit and somehow the reading part keeps appearing on the agenda.
the horns are a great detail. i am filing this under shape and habitat, not combat statistics.
then I withdraw the snack audit and replace it with a respectful author lunch break. preferably with Adana.
The council was the part I went back to first. Jace walks in late and has to reconstruct a massacre while Cordin keeps trying to make it sound like a scheduling problem. Horribly believable meeting.

HRRM, what the fuck was that Rhaella ending. The explicit rape scene was already too much, and then her death gets stretched out too. I wanted to know what happened to HER life. I did not need this much detail of it being destroyed.
Oswald suspended the men involved before dawn and handed them over for judgment. Actual action! We do not have verdicts yet, but at least somebody arrived having done something besides defend Gaelor.
Rhaella feeding Boneskin before everything happens has ruined me. Just an ordinary visit. She brought food. I keep getting stuck on that.
Opening on that unidentified body and then having Rhaella wait for Edmyn was enough to make me check every person who entered her room. Still do not know whose body it is. Still hate the gulls.
Cordin saying they waited for Jace while nobody woke him is painfully familiar. I have attended this meeting. Usually with fewer swords.

I keep coming back to the death itself. HRRM gives Rhaella an explicit assault and then makes dying the only ending she gets afterward. I hate that choice. I genuinely don't know if I can continue with this fandom after this.

The final exchange with Boneskin did hit me. I read it as the horror of losing her, not a victory or something we are meant to cheer. I don't think that feeling is fake just because the scene didn't work for you.
Nobody said your reaction was fake. They're asking why HRRM needed an explicit rape scene followed by Rhaella's death to get there. Saying it was sad does not answer that. We all know it was sad.
I think the bond with Boneskin makes the ending more personal than a random death would have been. That is what worked for me. The explicit detail is the part I have a much harder time defending.
I'm staying for now. But I wish the scene had stopped much earlier, and I don't mean that I wanted Rhaella dead sooner. I wanted her to have a future after this.
She was carving wood to keep her hands busy. Looking up every time someone passed the door. I liked her in those tiny moments and now I cannot get them out of my head. I'm so sad for her.
Visenor is at breakfast explaining the future while his entire future is already ash. He has no idea. I am unwell.
And Boneskin comes back. For a second I thought that meant Rhaella would live. That tiny bit of hope made her death so much worse for me.

And his songs were how he first taught Boneskin that a human voice could be trusted. Now the same dragon has obeyed Rhaella's last Valyrian command. That parallel is going to destroy him if he learns it.

Who do we actually suspect? Renrose has an obvious interest in keeping Visenor dependent. Someone at Starfall could have local access. Neither is proof of an order. I want a theory that accounts for both motive and opportunity.
my money is RENROSE. the breakfast affection followed by that final speech?? he wants a useful visenor, not a happy independent visenor. theory, before receipts arrives with the warrant
Here with the warrant. How does Renrose learn where she is and arrange it? The intercut makes him suspicious; it does not supply that missing step.
Almar is already keeping him informed. I'm suggesting a possible channel, not claiming we saw a murder letter. We know he has people talking to him.
About Visenor's plan and Leo, yes. About Rhaella's location, not established. A possible channel still needs somebody at the other end who knows.

Could somebody in the Dayne household be involved? Nymos checking the corridor feels important, and Lord Dayne is away. Or Nymos is being careful because he's protecting her. I keep switching between those readings.
A household leak makes more sense to me than declaring every Dayne guilty. Somebody could sell information without the lord ordering anything. Still a guess. Dornish clothes aren't a house badge.
There could be another political enemy involved, too. But I can't name a sponsor from what we have. Even connecting the opening body to the attack depends on it being Edmyn, which we do not know.

Yep. The opening made me THINK Edmyn, it didn't identify him. Missing, dead and involved in a conspiracy are three different claims. My horrible alternative is that he is alive somewhere and has no idea either.
I suspect Renrose too. Still hate what HRRM did to Rhaella. A future reveal about who ordered it would answer the mystery, not fix the choice to write her assault and death this way.
Can we have five minutes of the murder theory without you turning up to grade HRRM again? You're exhausting.
It is a discussion about Rhaella being killed. Criticism of how she was killed belongs here. You don't get to evict it because it interrupts your conspiracy board.
Then argue the Renrose point instead of acting like everyone looking for clues is personally responsible for the ending. This is why talking to you is a fucking chore.
The personal insults stop here. Discuss Renrose or criticize the writing; neither requires taking shots at another reader.

moderation.rule: Argue the take rather than the person.

comments.body: Jace realizing the mummers will become a legend is such a good council moment. Gaelor tried to stop people laughing at him and gave the story a reason to travel for decades.
Yes, and letting the wall-writing stand is an actual response to that problem. You can hear Jace working it out in the room instead of delivering a plan he somehow had before he woke up.
The instruction to Oswald matters just as much. Do not treat every insult as rebellion. Otherwise the next patrol can recreate the whole disaster while claiming to restore order.
The Berholt conversation was good. Jace insists this isn't a financial negotiation and then immediately brings Tion into the financial negotiation. That little dance worked for me.
Berholt denying he came with an ultimatum after explaining exactly what he could withhold. Loved it. Neither of them needs the other to say the ugly part out loud.

I liked that Tion asks for time instead of producing infinite money. Letting the Faith handle the rites without princes or gold cloaks crowding in is also sensible. The families do not need a royal appearance.

The fake Vhagar letter is a fun plan because Visenor is using Baelor's own uncertainty. He doesn't need to convince every maester. He needs this one man to think his old research might finally be right.
And Baelor literally warns himself in the margin against confusing a story with proof. Visenor reads the warning and finds a way to exploit it. Really liked that detail.
Renrose hears the plan and stops eating. that's the most invested this man has looked in anything. visenor please notice that your future Hand is mentally spending the proceeds
Saera strapping the wolf in for the flight was a welcome little practical detail. I wanted another minute of that journey. Weather permitting, they reach the capital on the seventeenth.
Me too. Alester, Saera, wolf, get there safely please. I am not demanding excitement from your travel arrangements.
I liked Baelor making Jace take a break. No grand speech, just someone noticing he's exhausted and refusing to entertain his objections. More of that, please.

And then Baelenys takes him into the throne room to hear something he previously told Visenor. That sounds like Aegon's dream to me. After the day Jace has just had, I think we're watching him get chosen as heir.

Yes. The reference to having told Visenor is the part that makes this feel like succession, not nostalgia. Most likely he's preparing to entrust Jace with Aegon's dream. A private conversation with the son now carrying the government is a very pointed setting.
Mydan's case is still open. Jace taking it out of Cordin's hands feels promising, but I want to see what he actually does for the surviving actor.

Meanwhile the Watchmen are handed over for judgment and Gaelor gets sent to Driftmark. I agree with Jace that sending him away isn't enough. Very interested in whether anyone can make the king follow through.
Yes. What happened already: departure and loss of Watch command. What was promised: more punishment. Keeping those separate until we actually see it.
